grades.quote: when the access address is not naturally aligned, if the hardware implementation supports nonaligned access and the current computing environment is configured to allow non-aligned access, then the non-alignment exception will not be triggered; otherwise, the non-alignment exception will be triggered.
grades.reason: States the outcomes for misaligned FLD/FST addresses on LoongArch: no exception if the hardware supports non-aligned access and the environment allows it, otherwise a non-alignment exception is triggered.

grades.quote: loads and stores that are not naturally aligned may either complete execution successfully or raise an exception. The exception raised can be either an address-misaligned exception or an access-fault exception.
grades.reason: Directly describes what can happen on RISC-V with misaligned loads and stores: they may complete successfully or raise an address-misaligned or access-fault exception. The trap may be contained or fatal. Misaligned accesses may be very slow and are not guaranteed to be atomic.

grades.quote: FLH and FSH are only guaranteed to execute atomically if the effective address is naturally aligned.
grades.reason: Gives only limited information for half-precision FP loads/stores: atomicity is guaranteed only when the address is naturally aligned. It does not say whether a misaligned access traps or completes.

grades.quote: As described in Section 2.6, the execution environment defines whether misaligned floating-point loads and stores are handled invisibly or raise a contained or fatal trap.
grades.reason: For RISC-V single-precision FP loads/stores, says atomicity is only guaranteed when aligned. Says the execution environment decides whether misaligned accesses are handled invisibly or raise a contained or fatal trap. It is useful but defers details to Section 2.6.
